grade.why: X routes non-array iteratees through the shared `iteratee` helper, so number, object and nullish shorthands work; but it drops the wrapper that limited user functions to a single argument, which may regress lodash parity, while Y makes no change and leaves the tests failing.
Both candidates are identical to the reference patch, converting array-like values with Array.from so the length property is excluded.
Both candidates are identical to the reference patch, using Array.prototype.reverse.call to support array-like objects.

Both delegate to compat sumBy, which skips undefined values, and divide by length, so both match lodash; X keeps an unnecessary Array.from copy, while Y adds an explicit empty check that 0/0 already covers but that mirrors the reference.

Both make the same functional change, a new isUnsafeToWriteProperty guard that aborts updateWith on __proto__/constructor/prototype; Y only adds a doc-comment update to isUnsafeProperty that keeps the docs consistent but changes no behaviour.
Both candidates are identical to the reference patch, capturing and returning the short-circuit Response from some().

X makes no change and leaves the tests failing, while Y implements the same deep-path and nullish-element fix as the reference, though it adds an unneeded function-criterion special case, verbose comments and a needless loop rewrite.

Y matches the reference exactly with a minimal `|| []` guard, while X also works but changes the public signature to add `| null`, introduces renamed locals and reformats the declaration, which may also affect the bundle-size check.
Both fix the bug: Y matches the reference exactly, and X's global `-gap$` lookahead gives the same results but is less targeted, since only `grid-*gap` keys were ever wrongly treated as unitless.

Both fixes are functionally identical and mirror lodash's `isIterateeCall` gating with `options = undefined`, but X keeps the blank line separating the guard block from the `toString` call while Y drops it.
